correctness.rationale: The exact ratio a/(b+1) and unit status force equal valuations j, with j<r since both a and b+1 are below p^r. Below j Lucas's no-carry criterion forces digits (0,p−1,0). At j the positive digits x of a and y of b+1 give quotient x/y and third digit in [0,p−x−y]; above j the digit triples are unchanged and there are Q_p choices per place. These conditions are sufficient too: the two decisive digit sums coincide, and the carry-free digits ensure n<p^r. This gives the geometric factor and, by stars and bars, the total binom(p+1,3)S_r. On replacing y by p−t, the permutation displacement formula gives N_p=p−1+sum(π(t)−t−1)_+. For multiplier −u other than 1, t=1 witnesses strictness if its representative is at least 3; t=2 witnesses it for representative 2 when p>=5. Away from u=−1, reflection pairs opposite nonzero displacements, giving N_p=(p−1)/2+F(π)/2. Summing crossings over all cuts bounds F by 2m² for m=(p−1)/2; saturation at the middle cut forces the halves to exchange, which then saturates every cut. This implies u stabilizes the lower half, whose sum is −1/8 mod p, so u=1. Direct p=3 gives the tie. In the binary restriction c=0, only x+y<=p matters: every y works at u=−1 and exactly one of each reflected pair works otherwise, so the reversal comparison is correct. My independent bounded Pascal recurrence builds the full trinomial rows modulo p and forms quotients from actual nonzero residues. All tested histograms match, including p=5,r=3 and p=11,r=2.
